about: Dev's coding in the reflexive thematic analysis demo (working from home), invented. Every participant turn in order, found by its opening words: each extract as said with its codes, and the passage's note, or empty for a turn reviewed and left uncoded. make_demo_rta.py builds the workbook and the progress file from this and the interview CSV beside it.

extracts.text: I was Dev from testing. People knew me.
I think I've sort of shrunk to fit it.
codes: No room that is only home

turns.note: Loss of a self, not of a place. Compare Toby, who never had one to lose.

extracts.text: I don't notice until Sam says, when did you last go out, properly.
codes: No room that is only home

extracts.text: I tidied the bit behind me for about a year.
Like my kitchen was going to be marked.
I walk out of my front door as a man in a flat, and I walk back in as, you know, someone at work.
codes: Small rituals to start and stop
The commute as a buffer, gone

extracts.text: I look up and it's six, and Sam's back, and I haven't moved.
I work longer now than I ever did in the office. Way longer.
At home, there's nobody packing up.
I've saved an hour and a half on the commute, so the bank's owed that hour and a half. Nobody's asked for it. I just give it.

turns.note: The saved time is felt as a debt. Glen says the same in other words.

turns.note: A man doing the gaps' work: the pattern follows who is at home, not who is a woman. Worth saying in the write-up.

extracts.text: Mostly I swallow it.
